info.bio: Hole es una banda de rock alternativo/grunge formada en Los Ángeles en  1989 por Courtney Love (voz, guitarra rítmica) y Eric Erlandson (guitarra). La banda ha logrado un éxito comercial y de crítica considerable a lo largo de la década de 1990, iniciando con el lanzamiento de sencillos a través de sellos independientes en Los Ángeles y debutando con su agresivo y influenciado noise rock Pretty on the Inside (1991), y más tarde ganando casi unánime aclamación de la crítica con su álbum de 1994, Live Through This.

scenes.name: Foxcore y riot grrrls
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El hardcore había sido un fenómeno masculino; el movimiento «riot grrrl» introduce el «factor chica» en la ecuación de frustración, depresión, desesperación y rabia. Nace en Olympia (fanzines como «Girl Germs», el lema «Revolution Girl Style Now!») y bebe de las cantautoras neoyorquinas, las bandas femeninas californianas (Runaways, Frightwig, L7) y las británicas (Raincoats, Slits). Un movimiento fundado en las letras, no en la música: Mecca Normal, Bikini Kill de Kathleen Hanna (y luego Le Tigre), Bratmobile, Team Dresch, Hole de Courtney Love, Seven Year Bitch, Sleater-Kinney. En California, Mudwimin, 4 Non Blondes, Tribe 8, Tiger Trap, Donnas, Red Aunts, That Dog, Muffs; en el Medio Oeste, Babes In Toyland (Fontanelle, «un arte de emociones extremas») y Sugarsmack; Free Kitten y Luscious Jackson en Nueva York.
scenes.family: Punk, new wave, hardcore y noise

podcast.title: Courtney Love's First Husband – Punk Transvestite Singer Falling James Moreland (1989)
podcast.body: Before marrying Kurt Cobain, Courtney Love had a drunken impulse-wedding in Las Vegas in 1989 with punk transvestite singer Falling James Moreland, the lead vocalist of the Leaving Trains (who had released albums on Black Flag's SST label). Moreland was the boyfriend of Jennifer Finch, who was about to join LA band L7. After sobering up, Courtney realized the mistake and they divorced within months. Moreland produced the first single for Courtney's new band, which was supposed to be called "Sweet Baby Crystal Powered by God" but was released as Hole — and the single was called "Retard Girl." "Listen, they've seen stranger things in Vegas."

podcast.title: Kristen Pfaff's Death (June 1994)
podcast.body: Kristen Pfaff, drummer for Hole, died in June 1994 from a drug overdose. "Kristen Faff, drummer for whole, Drug Overdose, June 1994."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: The Crow: Salvation Soundtrack Contribution (2000)
podcast.body: Hole contributed to *The Crow: Salvation* soundtrack, released in the spring of 2000. This album was associated with the sequel to *The Crow: City of Angels*, although the movie itself did not appear until 2004 and went straight to DVD. "More Hole, More Filter, Monster Magnet, Stabbing Westward, Kid Rock, Crystal Method."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Breast Flash at Wendy's (March 17, 2004) – St. Patrick's Day, Union Square, New York
podcast.body: On St. Patrick's Day 2004, an aspiring rapper named Kofi Assar was on his way to buy chicken nuggets at a Wendy's in Union Square, New York, when he encountered Courtney Love surrounded by paparazzi. He held the door for her; as she passed, he asked for "one last flash." Courtney pulled open her sheer white blouse — she was not wearing a bra — and Kofi kissed her right breast. Courtney smiled. Paparazzi photographed the entire encounter. Kofi leveraged the resulting worldwide news coverage to promote his rap career. "Naturally, the accumulated paparazzi were only too happy to take some pictures."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Accusation of Hitting on Frances Bean Cobain
podcast.body: Courtney Love publicly accused Dave Grohl of making advances toward her daughter with Kurt Cobain, Frances Bean Cobain. This accusation further escalated their feud, which spanned about 15 years and intensified with the rise of social media. "And then there was the time she accused Dave of hitting on Francis, Kurt and Courtney's daughter."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bausch & Lomb Inheritance – Courtney's Mother May Be Heir to $2 Billion Contact Lens Fortune
podcast.body: Courtney Love's mother, Linda Risi, was adopted by a wealthy San Francisco couple whose family controlled the Bausch & Lomb fortune. This wealth explains how Courtney's family could uproot and do things like start sheep farms in New Zealand when she was a child, and helped supplement Courtney's income during her pre-fame years working as a stripper. Bausch & Lomb currently generates annual revenues of approximately $2 billion. Unless Courtney has been written out of any wills due to her behavior, she stands to inherit a substantial further sum beyond the income she already receives from Kurt Cobain's estate. "It stands to reason that Courtney Love will one day inherit even more money."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Continuing Public Criticism and Apology
podcast.body: Courtney Love has consistently criticized Dave Grohl's public image, calling his reputation as "the nicest guy in rock" a "sham." In the summer of 2021, she posted a highly "incendiary" message about Dave Grohl and Trent Reznor on Instagram. Although the post was quickly deleted, it was followed by an apology where she expressed regret for being "insensitive and it was wrong" and committed to being more responsible with her words. "Courtney has said several times that Dave's reputation is the nicest guy in rock is a sham."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Feud with Dave Grohl
podcast.body: A significant and ongoing feud developed between Courtney Love and Dave Grohl following Kurt Cobain's death. The conflict began in earnest after Dave Grohl's 1999 interview where he implied Courtney Love did not write most of Hole's songs. Courtney then launched media attacks, accusing Grohl of being sexually obsessed with Kurt Cobain and claiming he hired Taylor Hawkins due to Hawkins' resemblance to Kurt. "It got ugly real fast with Courtney going after Dave in the media over various legal disputes involving Nirvana and the band's music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Founding with Carolyn Rue
podcast.body: Hole was founded with the help of Carolyn Rue, who once dated Eric Carlson, the guitarist for the punk band The Mentors (stage name Sikki Wifebeater). This connection played a role in Courtney Love meeting Elden Hoke, the frontman of The Mentors, a figure central to later conspiracy theories surrounding Kurt Cobain's death. "Carolyn Rue, help Courtney Love, found whole."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Heroin Decimation
podcast.body: Heroin tragically decimated and brought death to the band members of Hole. "Heroin decimated and brought death to the New York dolls. The pretenders sublime, smashing pumpkins, allyson chains, skinny puppy holes, Scott Wylin, D.D. Ramone, Billy Eidle, a chunk of ever-clear, a vast swath of the Britpop scene of the 1990s, and pretty much everyone who's ever been in the Red Hot Chili Peppers past in present."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Kristen Pfaff's Dream Machine Use and Death
podcast.body: After Kurt Cobain's death, Hole bassist Kristen Pfaff allegedly obtained the "dream machine" that Cobain had used. She began using it for long periods, against Courtney Love's wishes. By mid-June of the same year, Kristen Pfaff also died from a heroin overdose. "Shortly after Kurt's death, whole bases Christine Fath got a hold of the machine, and she began using it for long periods of time, again against the wishes of Courtney."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Love Triangle with Kurt Cobain and Billy Corgan
podcast.body: In the early 1990s, a love triangle reportedly existed between Courtney Love, Kurt Cobain, and Billy Corgan. After Kurt Cobain's death, Courtney and Billy Corgan briefly rekindled their relationship and then broke up. They reunited for a two-year period starting in 2006, leading to "hard feelings" that have since reportedly settled down. "For a while in the early 90s, there was something of a love triangle going on that also included Kurt Cobain."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Love vs. Barber vs. King – Three-Way Legal War Including Car-Over-Foot, Drugged Break-In, Assault with Liquor Bottle
podcast.body: Following a relationship with Geffen A&R executive Jim Barber, Courtney filed suit in December 2000 against his ex-wife Lesley Barber, alleging a 20-month campaign of stalking and harassment, including a plot to plant cocaine at Courtney's house and an incident on June 4, 2000, in which Lesley allegedly drove a Volvo over Courtney's foot outside her LA home — causing the injury that forced her withdrawal from a John Carpenter film. The lawsuit sought $1.5 million. In October 2003, Courtney was found by police trying to break into Jim's house while intoxicated on OxyContin; she was arrested on drug charges and ordered into rehab. Then, on April 25, 2004, Courtney arrived at Jim's house to find an unknown woman named Kristen King on the couch. Courtney pulled King's hair, scratched her, backhanded her in the face (breaking a tooth), tweaked her breasts, threw a lit candle at her, and struck her on the head with a liquor bottle. King called police; Courtney was charged with assault with a deadly weapon (the liquor bottle). Courtney paid a $1,000 fine, $2,750 in restitution, three years probation, one year of anger management, and 100 hours of community service. King filed a civil suit; a judge dismissed it in December 2006. "So here's a lesson, kids. Don't date Courtney or anyone who might have dated Courtney in the past."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Riot Grrrl Adjacent Band
podcast.body: Hole, featuring Courtney Love, is classified as "Riot Grrrl Adjacent," meaning they shared a kinship with the scene but were not formally part of it. These bands were often "a little more polished, not nearly as political and occasionally heavier and more riff happy" than core Riot Grrrl groups, appealing to a broader audience. "Well, L7, they were the lunatics, babes, and toilet, and most definitely, this band, Courtney Love and Whole."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Temporary Reconciliation at Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
podcast.body: A seemingly public reconciliation occurred between Courtney Love and Dave Grohl when they hugged at the 2014 Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony for Nirvana. However, underlying tension reportedly persisted. "There seemed to be some kind of public reconciliation when they hugged it out at the 2014 Rock and Roll Hall of Fame ceremony."
